tools.name: create_deliberation
tools.description:
Start a multi-model AI deliberation on a question or decision.

Runs the prompt through multiple frontier AI models in parallel and collects each model's typed reactions (KEEP/EXPLORE/CHALLENGE/CORE/SHIFT) to the others' claims, showing where they agree and diverge.

**Returns immediately (async).**

tools.name: ask_a_model
tools.description:
Put a question to ONE model of your choice and get its answer. Another lab's model typically makes for a better second opinion.

This is not a deliberation: there are no other models, so there are no cross-model reactions. For structured disagreement between 2–3 models, use `create_deliberation` ins

tools.name: append_round
tools.description:
Add a follow-up round to an existing deliberation session.

Use after you have summarized the previous round for the user and they have agreed to another round. Suggest one when a contested point could change the answer; do not append on your own. The `snippets` array carries your own reactions: spe

tools.name: wait_for_round
tools.description:
Wait for a deliberation round to finish, then return that round (not the whole session — `get_session` reads every round).

This is the follow-up to `create_deliberation`, `ask_a_model` and `append_round`: those tools return a fast ack; this tool polls the lightweight progress endpoint internally an

tools.name: get_session
tools.description:
Fetch a deliberation session: every visible round (its reacted-to claims grouped as Contested, Open, Pivotal and Kept, the takeaway when one was requested, then the responses), followed by the session details.

Use to re-read completed session state. While a round is running, prefer `wait_for_round`

tools.name: list_sessions
tools.description:
List the caller's deliberation sessions, optionally filtered by status.

Most useful for agents managing multiple concurrent sessions — use `status: 'ready'` to find sessions awaiting your next round. Returns a lightweight list (no response bodies); call `get_session` for full content.

tools.description: List the full model catalog, sorted by what your account can use: available on your plan, available on a higher plan, and unavailable right now (with the reason). findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "append_round" stacks urgency/override words (immediately, never, attention). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_deliberation, append_round, wait_for_round, get_session, share_session, get_credit · Private data: list_models, share_session, get_credit · Public sink: append_round, get_session, share_session, get_credit · Destructive: create_deliberation, wait_for_round, get_credit.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_deliberation, append_round, wait_for_round, get_session, share_session, get_credit · Private data: list_models, share_session, get_credit · Public sink: append_round, get_session, share_session, get_credit · Destructive: create_deliberation, wait_for_round, get_credit

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
